Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Agreement (1996, in force 2000)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (1967, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, transposing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD)); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20); CSSF Circular 18/698 on AML/CFT compliance; RBE operational via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) since 1 March 2019.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp Partnership Agreement (contrat de société) and any notarially certified signature specimens of the founding partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding partners and/or Luxembourg notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) for documents executed in Hague Contracting States, or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions; mandatory sworn translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish for RCS filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each natural-person partner, and certified extracts of the corporate register for any corporate partner/general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the partner's country of origin, registered corporate registry, and competent notarial body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn translation into French or German where required by the RCS

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Non-Impediment for each corporate partner, and certificate of incumbency confirming the signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce and Companies of the partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; sworn translation where requested by Luxembourg financial intermediaries or the RCS

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and documented source of funds of each partner (where the partnership opens a Luxembourg bank account)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding credit institution of the partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn translation into French or German; apostille generally not required for bank correspondence, but certified by the issuing bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and verification of Beneficial Owners and all natural-person partners, including mandatory screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated lists, Luxembourg national asset-freeze measures, OFAC SDN list (as international best practice for cross-border and USD-related flows), and CSSF AML/CFT guidance; mandatory enhanced due diligence for everything equivalent to politically exposed persons (PEPs) under the Law of 12 November 2004; permanent adverse-media and sanctions re-screening protocols must be embedded in the Canadian de-risking? No—standard AML/CFT internal policies applicable to an SCSp with no regulated status but subject to RBE verification by its obligated intermediaries (banks, notaries, PSPs, and auditors).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - www.lbr.lu, including the e-RCS electronic filing platform and online name availability search
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script; French, German, and Luxembourgish are the official working languages, although other EU-language names are admissible at the RCS; the SCSp name must include the words 'société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' immediately following or preceding the distinctive element; names must not create confusion with existing RCS-registered entities and must not violate Luxembourg public order (ordre public) or misleading advertising rules
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection by the LBR, the applicant may file a reasoned written objection with the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 working days of notification; if the refusal is maintained, the applicant may petition the Chambre Commerciale (Commercial Chamber) of the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg within 30 days, pursuant to Article 13 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; the court ruling is final at first instance subject to an ordinary appeal to the Cour d'Appel within 40 days; practical practice: immediate re-filing under an amended distinctive element normally resolves commercial blockage without judicial recourse.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a low-risk, non-regulated SCSp through a duly licensed professional domiciliation provider in Luxembourg; the central administration and decision-making records must remain traceable to the registered office, and the RCS requires a verifiable Luxembourg address; virtual office alone does not satisfy tax residence or substance expectations for treaty benefits and must be accompanied by adequate economic substance (board/minute records, accounting, operational oversight) relative to ISIC 6201 app development activity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (the 1915 Law), as amended by the law of 23 July 2016, notably Articles 944-16 to 944-26 instituting the Société en commandite spéciale (SCSp); Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 sur le registre de commerce et des sociétés et les comptes annuels (RCS law); Loi modifiée du 2 septembre 2011 réglementant l'accès aux professions d'artisan, de commerçant, d'industriel et à certaines professions libérales (establishment permit regime); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 September 2016 on environmental impact assessment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 1-3 rue de la Forêt, L-2929 Luxembourg; electronic filing portal at lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Statuts / Contrat de Société) in notarial or private-writing form, filed with the RCS; mandatory legal notice published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations); registration certificate (extrait) issued by the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital requirement for an SCSp; contributions and payment terms are freely determined in the Partnership Agreement. No Luxembourg escrow account is required for cash contributions. In-kind contributions consisting of registered assets must be certified by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises and effected by notarial deed where asset registration law so requires. The General Partner bears unlimited liability; each Limited Partner's liability is capped at its agreed capital contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Subscribers of the SCSp, acting as a constitutive meeting, hereby resolve: First, the Partnership Agreement is adopted, and each Limited Partner's subscription to capital interests is accepted, with contributions committed as set forth therein. Second, the registered office is established at [Address], L-0000 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and may be relocated by subsequent resolution of the Manager. Third, [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant), with sole authority to represent the SCSp, file RCS registrations, open bank accounts, engage legal, tax and corporate services providers, and perform all acts necessary to complete formation, publication, beneficial-owner filing and regulatory licensing, including delegation of day-to-day administration where appropriate. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) for notarial deed; alternatively private-writing execution signed by all partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Partnership Agreement in French or English (with a certified French translation) containing the SCSp name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate object covering software development and mobile utility applications (ISIC 6201), the General Partner with unlimited liability, Limited Partners with their commitments, manager provisions, duration and profit-sharing rules. Convene a notarial appointment; all partners or their attorneys-in-fact must appear before the notary, verify identity and legal existence, and execute the deed. If private-writing execution is chosen, all parties sign every page and the date is certified; however, a notarial deed is recommended to facilitate KYC and RCS acceptance. The notary authenticates the certified copies used for filing.
required_dossiers: Approved draft of the SCSp Partnership Agreement (Statuts)
Valid passport or national identity card of each natural-person partner
Certificate of good standing and board resolution of each corporate partner authorizing the subscription
Proof of address of each partner not older than three months
Registered office consent letter or subordination agreement signed by the office provider
AML/KYC declarations and source-of-funds statements for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the parties' compliance review raises queries, cure by revising the draft, obtaining the missing KYC documents and rescheduling the execution; since no registry filing has yet occurred, no adverse registry consequence arises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the online portal lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the LBR portal and select the new company registration flow. Enter the exact legal form Societé en commandite spéciale (SCSp), the proposed name, registered office address, corporate object (software development and mobile utility services), duration, General Partner, Limited Partners, manager and the SCSp's mode of representation. Upload the notarial certified copy of the Partnership Agreement, the manager's identification and criminal-record extract, proof of the appointed manager, the office-holder consent and the AML documentation. Pay the EUR 75 filing fee by credit card or SEPA. The RCS verifies name availability and legal compliance within five business days, assigns the registration number and issues the extraction certificate; archive the RCS extract for all subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the executed Partnership Agreement
Extract from the Luxembourg criminal record (casier judiciaire) of the Manager issued within the last three months
Written consent of the registered office holder
Certified French/German translation of any non-Luxembourg official document
Power of attorney granted to the Luxembourg filing agent if applicable
Proof of payment of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refusal, remediate by amending the Partnership Agreement or curing the document deficiencies identified in the RCS notice within the statutory three-month window and refile electronically; the filing fee is retained for the corrected resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the registration notice in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS approval, the RCS automatically transmits the legal notice to the RESA for electronic publication. No separate applicant action is normally required. Verify the published notice for exact legal name, legal form, registered office, partners' liability regime, manager identity, object and RCS number; request a rectification of any typographical or substantive error within eight days. If third-party effect is time-critical, request a written confirmation from the RCS showing the date of registration and publication.
required_dossiers: No separate dossier - the RCS generates the notice
Copy of the RCS registration extract for verification
Optional certified translation of the RESA notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice contains inaccurate data, file a rectification request with the RCS via the online portal; the corrected notice is republished and becomes opposable to third parties from the corrected publication date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Beneficial Owners in the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE) department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the beneficial owner declaration electronically in the RBE. Identify each Limited Partner owning or controlling at least 25% of capital, voting rights or profits and each natural person who ultimately owns or controls a corporate partner, including full name, date of birth, nationality, residential address, tax identification number and the nature and extent of the beneficial interest. Describe the chain of ownership for indirect holders. Confirm the declaration by the Manager; update the RBE within one month of any change in beneficial ownership.
required_dossiers: Electronic RBE declaration form (signed by the Manager)
Share register or ownership schedule of the SCSp and of any corporate partners
Identification data of each ultimate beneficial owner
Description of the chain of control for indirect owners
Certified extract of the register of shareholders of any foreign corporate partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE queries the declaration, promptly clarify the ownership chain and file an amended declaration; late or inaccurate declarations are subject to fines, so any correction must be submitted without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and VAT registration with the Luxembourg authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Tax Authorities; filing via Guichet.lu secured portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the national VAT registration request (form 640) for the SCSp together with the application for the national business number (matricule). Provide a Luxembourg fiscal domicile address and state the intended accounting period. For the app-store freemium model, describe the payment rails (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing) and the platform contracts so the AEDT can determine the place-of-supply treatment of digital supplies under EU VAT rules. Upon completion, the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT number and opens the direct tax file for the transparent partnership; the General Partner is responsible for filing returns.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (certified copy)
Partnership Agreement
Identification documents of the Manager and General Partner
VAT registration form LCNL 640
Proof of Luxembourg registered office
Bank account details of the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT requests clarification on cross-border digital supplies or the VAT regime of the SCSp, submit a reasoned explanation letter with the app-store contracts; if no response is received within five working days, escalate to the competent AEDT VAT bureau.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction Générale de l'Économie / Middle Office; application submitted via Guichet.lu or in paper form to the Ministry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing commercial invoicing, apply for the establishment permit required for pursuing the software and application development activity. Submit the RCS extract, the Manager's clean criminal record, evidence of professional competence (diploma in computer science or equivalent professional experience of at least three years in software development), the social security registration certificate, and the lease or ownership title of the Luxembourg registered office. The Ministry examines the application and issues the permit or a conditional response; retain the permit for bank KYC, app-store account vetting and future administrative filings.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Criminal record extract of the Manager issued within three months
Diplomas or professional evidence for the Manager
Social security registration certificate (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale - CCSS)
Identity documents of the Manager and General Partner
Lease agreement or title deed of the registered office
Description of the activities and business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry raises a query, submit supplemental documentation within the deadline stated in the query; an unfavorable decision can be appealed to the Tribunal administratif within three months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational safety and civil-defense clearance of the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); communal building and occupancy authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the Luxembourg registered office and any physical workplace, verify the building occupancy permit with the landlord and ensure structural load compliance. Arrange a fire safety inspection by the CGDIS covering exit routes, fire extinguishers and emergency lighting. Complete the single risk assessment document (document unique) under the Luxembourg Labour Code and register the workplace with the ITM; declare all employees to the CCSS before engagement. Keep all clearance certificates on file and affix the statutory safety notices in the premises.
required_dossiers: Workplace risk assessment (document unique)
Fire safety inspection report and certificate from the CGDIS
Building occupancy permit (autorisation d'exploitation) delivered by the commune
Lease agreement and landlord consent
Staff declarations to the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
ITM workplace registration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ITM or CGDIS issues observations, implement corrective measures within the imposed deadline, request reinspection and obtain a clearance certificate; continued non-compliance can result in administrative fines or suspension of the establishment permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction Générale de l'Économie / Middle Office (authority delivering the establishment permit for commercial, craft and industrial activities).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to craft, commercial, industrial and certain liberal professions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category D (services / software only). No environmental impact assessment report and no prior classified-installation authorisation are required under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 September 2016 because the mobile utility software activity creates no physical industrial installation; only ordinary municipal waste and office-compliance duties apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the software-only SCSp. Office wastewater discharges to the municipal sewer pursuant to commune discharge rules; no industrial VOC or other emission thresholds apply. End-of-life IT and electrical equipment must be disposed of through approved WEEE channels under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 2012 on electrical and electronic equipment waste, and non-hazardous office waste must be collected by an authorised waste operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the CGDIS for the registered office and any workplace (Class B low-occupancy office, fire extinguishers, unobstructed exit routes and emergency signage); building structural-load and occupancy permit approved by the competent communal authority; workplace safety clearance from the ITM after completion of the single risk assessment; mandatory registration of employees with the CCSS for social security coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT and registration; official single portal: guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Registry (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) through a Luxembourg domicile agent to obtain an RCS number. Step 2: Apply to the ACD for the Luxembourg national identification number (NIF) for the SCSp. Step 3: Apply separately to the AED for a VAT ID using the 'Déclaration d'inscription à la TVA' (VAT 100) via the MyGuichet electronic portal. Because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, each partner must obtain its own NIF; the SCSp obtains a NIF for administrative filing purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg CIT purposes; profits are allocated directly to partners. Resident partners are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg real estate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under Article 178 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR), a transparent partnership may elect, under limited conditions, to be jointly taxed as a corporate body. Other statutory elections include the VAT group election (assujetti unique), the IP box regime election (80% exemption of qualifying IP income), and the notional interest deduction (NID) election. The SCSp does not have a direct U.S.-style check-the-box election, but hybrid mismatch treatment is governed by Luxembourg implementation of the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) under Luxembourg VAT Law and EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-business exemption (Article 57 Luxembourg VAT Law); no registration threshold applies to non-established foreign suppliers, who must register after the first taxable supply in Luxembourg, subject to EU distance-sales and OSS rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or government digital stamping system. B2B e-invoicing is permitted with recipient consent. B2G e-invoicing has been mandatory since 1 June 2020 for invoices to the central Luxembourg administration using the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format. VAT returns and EU recapitulative statements are filed electronically through the AED's eCDF portal. Luxembourg is preparing for the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) digital reporting and e-invoicing framework, but no continuous transaction control mandate is yet operational.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods supplied from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU may be zero-rated provided the goods physically leave the EU within the prescribed timeline and the supplier retains full documentary evidence of export. Digital services and mobile utility applications supplied to non-EU customers (B2B or B2C) fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT because the place of supply is outside the EU; this requires documentary substantiation of the customer's non-EU status (e.g., IP address, business registration records, OECD residence certificate). To claim zero-rating on goods, the exporter must hold an EORI number, lodge a customs export declaration, and maintain the export contract/order.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation via Douanes Luxembourg)
Bill of Lading (ocean), CMR (road) or Air Waybill (air)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank evidence of receipt of export proceeds)
Commercial invoice with Incoterms and export reason code
International contract / purchase order from the non-EU buyer
Proof of EU exit (customs endorsed export movement document, e.g., T2L, T1, or AEF)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities may retrospectively disallow export zero-rating and claw back VAT, plus late payment interest at the current annual statutory rate of 8%. Administrative fines may reach EUR 10,000 per invoice or up to 100% of the evaded tax in cases of gross negligence. Intentional fraudulent export zero-rating is a criminal offence under Article 397 of the General Tax Code, punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years, monetary penalties, and an extended 10-year limitation period running from discovery of the fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) with prudential oversight by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); foreign exchange policy is governed by the European Central Bank (ECB) within the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-zone member with full capital and current account convertibility. No exchange controls, no profit remittance restrictions, and no tax withholding on dividends or interest under EU directives for qualifying entities. Remittance of profits from a SCSp is treated as a distribution to partners and is not subject to withholding tax in Luxembourg; however, banking compliance and anti-money-laundering obligations apply. In exceptional national-security or EU sanctions cases, temporary capital restrictions could be activated, but none are currently in force.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion rules exist in Luxembourg. Export receipts and all commercial receivables may be retained in EUR or freely converted into any other currency. The SCSp may hold multi-currency accounts without central bank approval. No mandatory conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account and Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Operational Multi-Currency Account and Capital Escrow Sub-Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Account and Segregated Capital Escrow Wing

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Quintet Private Bank (formerly KBL European Private Bankers)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-Currency Treasury Account with FX Hedging Capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for EU-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under PSD2 for daily collection from app stores (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing) and low-value cross-border disbursements. Limitations: EMIs cannot extend credit, hold client funds as term deposits, or provide full treasury/liquidity management; they also lack the robustness of SWIFT-backed clearing for large capital injection or trade settlement. The SCSp should use an EMI as a secondary payment gateway, not as the primary treasury bank. Legal constraint: EMI passports must be validated in Luxembourg and the EMI must comply with CSSF AML/CFT outsourcing requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks generally require a physical presence of at least one partner or duly appointed agent (mandataire) for the initial KYC interview and signature cards. Remote onboarding is permitted only through digital video identification and must comply with CSSF Regulation 12-02; however, most relationship managers request at least one in-person meeting at the bank's Luxembourg branch, especially when the SCSp has non-resident partners. Fully remote opening may be possible for low-risk fintech clients but is not guaranteed and often takes longer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex partnership structure with multiple non-resident silent partners and nominee interests
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved SCSp partnership agreement; fully updated register of partners with legal names and addresses; authenticated UBO declarations for all partners holding 10% or more; detailed organizational chart linking all intermediate legal vehicles; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for each partner; professional reference letters from approved AML advisors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border app business with high-volume micro-transactions originating from multiple jurisdictions and app stores
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed mobile utility app terms of service and privacy policy; Apple and Google developer agreements; historical monthly transaction reports and settlement reports; business continuity policy and transaction monitoring policy; liability insurance certificates (cyber and professional indemnity); periodic audited or unaudited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Neo-entity with no tax filing history and no prior audited financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward-looking business plan with revenue and traffic metrics; capitalization table and proof of seed capital injection; representation letter from a Luxembourg-certified chartered accountant (Réviseur d'entreprises); agreed tax compliance plan (including pass-through status under Luxembourg tax law); undertaking to provide annual financial statements within statutory deadlines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from high-risk jurisdictions or sanctions-adjacent investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent compliance screening report proving absence of sanctioned entities; notarized beneficial ownership declarations with commitment to notify changes within 30 days; legal opinion from a Luxembourg attorney on partnership law; wire transfer origin explanation with supporting bank statements from the investor's regulated bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the overseas investor's regulated banking institution to the SCSp's Luxembourg IBAN. Recommended purpose codes: 'INVEST' (Investment) or 'PCAP' (Capital Contributions) according to the ECB's purpose code classification. The receiving bank will require the capital contribution to match the subscribed amounts in the partnership agreement. For non-EUR transfers, the sending bank performs FX conversion at issue, or the SCSp may instruct the receiving bank to convert using the ECB reference rate. All inbound transfers must be accompanied by a detailed remittance instruction containing the SCSp full legal name, partner name, and partnership agreement article referencing the contribution. Enhanced due diligence is required for transfers above EUR 10,000 or from third-country high-risk jurisdictions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The SCSp's outbound clearing rails should consist of: (1) SWIFT MT103 for recurring operating payments, license fees, royalties, and subcontractor settlements; (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) for any physical infrastructure procurement or significant commercial contracts, primarily unconfirmed and issued by the Luxembourg financial institution; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for all euro-denominated intra-EU payments below EUR 100,000, as this offers lower fees and immediate settlement. For app store disbursements, funds are generally accumulated in the app store's clearing house and settled on a net basis via ACH or SWIFT to the designated bank account. The SCSp should designate a single primary treasury bank to aggregate all inbound and outbound flows and maintain real-time FX sweeping for currency exposures.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forwards (under ISDA Master Agreement or local European master agreement)
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF non-deliverable forwards for speculative- and trade-related hedges
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for maturity-matched principal exchanges
European-style FX options on EUR pairs used exclusively for downside protection
FX swaps for short-term liquidity management between the SCSp's operational and escrow accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation declaration (RBE annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year; official RBE confirmation window is 1 January to 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation triggers court-ordered coercive fines and possible suspension of RCS filing access; repeated default may lead to RBE registration strike-off and manager liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS registration-data confirmation and continuation-of-activity declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within the calendar-year confirmation window (generally 1 January to 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm may result in an RCS formal demand, administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) after repeated non-compliance, and dissolution without liquidation procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements); public RCS filing mandatory only for large or non-exempt partnerships
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) with publication via RESA; internal records if filing exemption applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing for entities subject to filing triggers RCS summons, fines up to EUR 1,000, default assessment pressure from tax authorities, and eventual strike-off; exempt small SCSp must still prepare and retain accounts for partners and tax authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return and partnership income-allocation declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des Contributions Directes – ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 September of the following tax year for 31 December year-end, subject to extension via e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to 10% of assessed tax; taxation d'office (default assessment) if the return is not filed; statutory late payment interest and administrative fines up to EUR 1,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recurring VAT returns, EC Sales List, and annual Luxembourg VAT recapitulative declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT – Luxembourg VAT Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly VAT returns due by the 12th day of the following month; quarterly returns due by the 20th day after quarter-end; annual EC Sales List by 31 January after the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return fines per unreported period, default interest on VAT due, and administrative penalties assessed by the AEDT; intentional non-filing may expose officers to criminal fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for a Luxembourg SCSp if it qualifies as a large undertaking under two of three thresholds at balance-sheet date: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, average workforce above 50 employees. SCSp structures operating as regulated AIF/RAIF fund vehicles require a CSSF-approved independent auditor irrespective of size. The partnership agreement may also impose an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and related Grand-Ducal regulations; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted where applicable for consolidated or voluntarily for non-listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners and submit UBO declarations to the RBE at registration and on any change in ultimate ownership. Partnership-interest transfers or share transfers do not by themselves trigger a public re-filing unless the identity of beneficial owners changes; however, the entity must annually confirm the accuracy of RBE data using the official RBE annual-confirmation procedure. If a transfer alters beneficial ownership, a fresh UBO filing must be made within one month of knowledge of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Registre des associés / limited-partner register)
Register of Managers/Gérants (manager decisions and appointments register)
Minute Book (records of partner resolutions and management resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 4,000 per year (Luxembourg domiciliation and registered-agent services, including compliance mailbox and annual RCS/RBE confirmation handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 12,000 per audit engagement for a small or medium undertaking; USD 8,000 – 25,000 for CSSF-supervised fund or significantly larger balance-sheet structures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% base CIT for fiscal year 2024/2025, plus a 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT and municipal business tax at a maximum of 6.75% in Luxembourg City, producing a combined top statutory burden of approximately 24.94%. The SCSp itself is fiscally transparent; no CIT is levied at the SCSp level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains on participations of at least 10% or with an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million held for at least 12 months. IP Box: 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income under the modified nexus approach. The mobile utility app developer may claim ordinary business cost deductions, R&D and digital investment incentives if applicable, but no statutory tax holiday exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 - Luxembourg annual combined corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax return. Electronic filing via the ACD eTax portal (MyGuichet.lu) using eCDF.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due for each fiscal year by 31 December of the assessment year; the initial filing deadline is 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end, extendable to 31 December when the fiscal year corresponds to the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS registration number, LEI, registered office address and Luxembourg tax identification number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not filed by a non-resident partner; the resident corporate partner completes its own Form 100 and includes the SCSp profit share. A non-resident partner with a Luxembourg PE files Form 100A instead.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period; usually a 12-month period ending 31 December.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners use their own fiscal year for home-country reporting and should align the Luxembourg assessment to the same accounting period where treaty relief is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form code identifying the entity as a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), fiscally transparent partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident partner is not required to enter the SCSp legal form; the partner uses its own corporate legal form code in its own jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the allocable share of SCSp net income: app store gross receipts less platform commissions (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing), development costs, support costs, marketing costs and financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner with a Luxembourg PE attributes the app-related profit allocable to Luxembourg and files Form 100A; the PE must apply OECD digital economy attribution rules to the mobile app user contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare the amount of prior-year tax losses offset against current-year SCSp profit. Losses may be carried forward for 17 years (from FY 2017 onwards; pre-2017 losses remain unlimited).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses incurred in the SCSp are included in the transparent partner's profit share and are governed by the partner's home country loss rules; the Luxembourg ACD does not automatically allow cross-border loss transfer absent a PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: ACD may impose an increased assessment under Article 169 LIR, a tax surcharge up to 20% of assessed tax, and monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%. Wilful evasion can trigger criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment up to five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100A - Luxembourg non-resident corporate income tax return. Electronic filing via ACD eTax / MyGuichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same annual cycle as Form 100: due by 31 December of the assessment year; initial deadline 31 March following the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name of the non-resident corporate partner, country of residence, foreign tax ID and Luxembourg PE registration reference if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Form 100A instead of Form 100; attach the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the partner's tax authority to support treaty benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate Luxembourg-source business profit from the SCSp and from the mobile app's in-app payment streams, net of traceable expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The OECD/UN digital economy provisions determine whether app-store revenue is attributable to a Luxembourg PE; if no PE exists, no Luxembourg CIT return filing is required for the foreign partner, and any SCSp allocation is generally treated as outside Luxembourg taxing scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: DTA reduction or exemption on Luxembourg-source income, with the applicable treaty article and supporting TRC annexed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim relief under the applicable DTA; in the absence of a Luxembourg PE, business profits are typically not taxable in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report any Luxembourg dividend WHT on dividends received from a capital-company subsidiary held by the SCSp and claim exemption under the participation exemption or Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp's distributions are non-withholding profit allocations; only the underlying capital-company dividend is subject to WHT, which is generally 0% where participation exemption conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Identical late-filing and evasion sanctions as Form 100; the non-resident partner also loses the procedural benefit of treaty claims when documents are not timely supplied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual SCSp transparency information statement - partner allocation schedule submitted to the ACD with the Form 100/100A return (administrative schedule, electronic PDF through MyGuichet.lu).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: To be filed concurrently with the partners' returns: by 31 March following the fiscal year-end, extendable to 31 December of the assessment year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A - Partner identity and allocation percentages
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names, addresses, tax identification numbers and profit/loss sharing ratios of the general partner and limited partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-limited partners should provide TRCs and a short explanation of their tax transparency treatment to avoid information exchange queries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of mobile app gross revenue by platform, platform commission deductions, operating expenses, net profit or loss for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a breakdown of in-app purchases by country of user download if requested by the ACD for PE attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of Luxembourg employees, director residences, minutes of board meetings held in Luxembourg, IT infrastructure hosting location, Luxembourg bank account details and outsourced service agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document an actual commercial decision-making function in Luxembourg to withstand GAAR challenges and preserve the tax transparent outcome.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Refusal to supply the partner allocation statement may be sanctioned by the ACD's discretionary assessment, reversal of the burden of proof and an administrative fine up to EUR 25,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax for dividends distributed by a Luxembourg capital company. In the SCSp, profit distributions to partners are not statutory dividends and are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax because the SCSp is fiscally transparent and has no CIT personality. Where the SCSp holds shares in an operating company, dividends from that company qualify for 0% WHT under the Luxembourg participation exemption or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (≥10% holding or ≥ EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost and ≥12 months holding).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain DTA relief, the corporate partner must: (1) obtain an official Luxembourg Tax Residency Certificate from the ACD; (2) complete a 'Demande d'attestation de résidence' with the partner's local tax office; (3) submit the Form 100A and annex a copy of the relevant DTA article, TRC, and proof of ownership of the SCSp interest; (4) for dividends paid by a capital-company subsidiary, file a withholding tax exemption application with the ACD before the dividend is distributed; (5) maintain the 12-month holding period and demonstrate beneficial ownership. Payments from the transparent SCSp require no WHT procedure, but the ultimate distribution of dividends from any underlying Luxembourg operating SA/S.à r.l. must follow the standard 0% WHT route.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory Luxembourg WHT on corporate interest payments (no gateway WHT on outbound interest). Royalties: 0% statutory Luxembourg WHT on IP royalties (royalties are not taxed at source unless attributable to a Luxembourg PE). In-app sale proceeds and app-store licensing revenue are treated as business profits rather than royalties; therefore no Luxembourg source WHT applies in the absence of a PE. Treaties generally preserve a 0% rate where a Luxembourg capital company pays interest or royalties to a DTA resident, though the Luxembourg payer must meet the anti-abuse / beneficial ownership standard.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million consolidated group turnover for the Master File; EUR 15 million annual Luxembourg entity turnover for the Local File. Groups with consolidated turnover of at least EUR 750 million must also file a Country-by-Country Report under OECD/EU CbCR requirements. In practice, the ACD may request arm's-length documentation for any related-party transaction even below these thresholds, particularly where mobile app IP royalties or intragroup development fees are present.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a bespoke Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE or Cayman Islands. Substance is nevertheless enforced through the Luxembourg GAAR under LIR Article 6, ATAD interest limitation rules, the DAC6 mandatory disclosure regime and the OECD principal-purpose test. An SCSp developing a mobile utility app must show real substance in Luxembourg: local offices, employees, active management decisions, a Luxembourg bank account, local accounting and IP ownership aligned with functions, assets and risks. Absent substance, the ACD may recharacterise the arrangement as artificial, deny tax treaty benefits and impose taxes with interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting Apple IAP or Google Play Billing revenue, hiding advertising income, or failing to declare the SCSp profit share on the corporate partner's Form 100.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax increase up to 20% under Article 169 LIR, late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of one month to five years under Luxembourg criminal tax law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are jointly liable for restitution of evaded taxes and may face travel bans, asset freezes, and in criminal cases imprisonment; the corporate veil will be pierced where the SCSp was used as a fraud facade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Luxembourg SCSp without offices, staff or commercial decision-making, while mobile app development and customer contracts are managed abroad, solely to achieve tax transparency and 0% withholding on app-store profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD recharacterises the structure under LIR Article 6 and assesses tax at the real owner at the combined 24.94% rate, plus 10% statutory annual interest and a concealment surcharge of up to 50%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused or benefited from the artificial structure may be personally liable for the additional taxes assessed against the company, with civil restitution ordered by the Luxembourg administrative courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the SCSp's beneficial owners with the Luxembourg RBE register or allowing the app's in-app payment rails to process suspicious funds without proper AML/KYC controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to EUR 5 million for legal persons, suspension of commercial activities for up to 10 years, public naming of sanctions and FIU penalties; suspicious transaction reports are mandatory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and directors may be imprisoned for six months to five years, receive travel bans and personal fines up to EUR 250,000; the corporate veil is pierced in AML offences where the SCSp was the instrumentality of money laundering.
